summary: Wall Street posted its best day since April 2025 as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang and jumped 31%, a relief rally after a heavy rout; NY Fed's Williams stayed hawkish on inflation, oil slid on surplus fears and gold bounced off a 14-month low.
events_next_24h: Wed 2:00am USD CB Consumer Confidence (Nov) — Forex Factory feed unavailable this run, check the calendar
tier1_next_14d: US PCE and personal income (Oct) + Q3 GDP 2nd estimate · Thu, 26 Nov, 12:30am

ES.why: Best day since April 2025 on Nvidia's CEO reinstatement, but VIX near 36, hawkish Williams and funds crowded long (94th pct) cap the case.
ES.risk: Follow-through buying into PCE would turn this bullish.

NQ.why: Nasdaq jumped ~6% as Nvidia rose 31% on Jensen Huang's return, lifting the AI overhang; funds lean long (85th pct) and vol is extreme.
NQ.risk: A fade of Monday's gains or hot PCE Thursday flips it.

YM.why: Dow rallied ~1,400 points in a relief bounce, but a hawkish Fed and record-high vol leave one day of buying unproven.
YM.risk: Second day of broad gains would tilt bullish.

RTY.why: Small caps join the bounce, but Williams says the Fed has work to do on inflation and higher 2-year yields hurt rate-sensitive firms.
RTY.risk: Softer PCE and falling yields would favour small caps.

NKD.why: Nikkei tracks the US AI rebound after a 10% monthly drop; fund positioning is neutral (32nd pct), so room to add, but vol is very high.
NKD.risk: Renewed US tech selling or sharp yen strength would flip it.

6E.why: Euro data are resilient and ECB hike talk supports it, but the dollar sits near a 19-month high on Fed hike bets.
6E.risk: A soft PCE weakening the dollar would favour the euro.

6J.why: USD/JPY sits near 160 with Tokyo warning on moves and a BOJ hike expected in Dec, against a hawkish Fed and risk-on mood.
6J.risk: Intervention or hawkish BOJ talk lifts 6J fast; hot PCE sinks it.

6B.why: Sterling edged higher but no clear UK catalyst; dollar strength on Fed hike bets offsets it.
6B.risk: A decisive dollar move after PCE sets the direction.

6A.why: Risk-on rebound helps the Aussie, but the strong dollar and falling commodity prices like oil weigh on it.
6A.risk: Sustained equity gains with a softer dollar would tilt bullish.

ZN.why: Williams says inflation stays above 2% until 2028 and 2-year yields jumped as stocks rebounded, pressuring Treasury prices.
ZN.risk: Soft PCE or a renewed stock rout would send bonds higher.

GC.why: Gold bounced ~2.5% from a 14-month low with funds leaning short (20th pct), but Fed hike bets and a firm dollar still weigh.
GC.risk: Hawkish PCE resumes the slide; dovish data extends the bounce.

CL.why: Brent fell over 3% below $90 as Middle East flows recover and surplus fears grow; funds are crowded short (10th pct), so squeeze risk.
CL.risk: New Gulf shipping attacks or supply disruption would spark a short squeeze.
